Imagine waking up to 100,000 security alerts overnight and having to figure out which one is the real attack. That’s exactly why AI Cyber Analysts are becoming essential in modern cybersecurity teams. AI can scan millions of signals, but it still needs skilled analysts to decide what actually matters and what to ignore.

An AI Cyber Analyst blends traditional cybersecurity skills with AI‑powered threat detection. You still need strong foundations in networking, SIEM platforms like Splunk or QRadar, endpoint detection tools, IDS/IPS systems, and incident response workflows. Core skills like log analysis, packet inspection, scripting in Python or PowerShell, and understanding of common attack techniques are non‑negotiable. You’re still doing investigations, triage, and incident response—but now with much smarter tools.

description:
An Analytics Manager plays a crucial role in any data-driven organization by overseeing the collection, analysis, and interpretation of data to help guide strategic decision-making. This role is responsible for ensuring that business operations, marketing efforts, customer behavior, and other areas are optimized based on data insights. The Analytics Manager helps organizations make informed, evidence-based decisions to improve performance, reduce costs, and drive growth.

Core Responsibilities

The primary duty of an Analytics Manager is to collect and analyze data from various sources to generate actionable insights. This involves overseeing data collection processes to ensure that the right data is gathered, and it is accurate and reliable. The manager is responsible for using analytical tools and techniques to evaluate trends and create meaningful reports. These reports can help identify areas for optimization, predict future trends, and support business strategies.

In 2026, just knowing how to code is not enough. If you want to become a great software engineer, you need to understand System Design. This skill helps you build large applications that can handle millions of users smoothly.

Top companies like Amazon, Netflix, Spotify, and Google look for engineers who know how to design scalable systems. With AI, cloud computing, and large platforms growing rapidly, System Design has become one of the most important skills for developers.

In this video, we talk about the System Design roadmap for 2026 and the key concepts every developer should learn. This includes data storage, sharding, replication, caching, load balancing, cloud architecture, microservices, and AI-driven systems like LLMs and RAG pipelines.

If you want to build powerful applications and stand out as a developer, learning System Design is a must. Start your System Design journey today and prepare for high-level engineering roles.
